classification.difficultyReason: Use equal perpendicular radii to find two corner-to-centre distances, add the touching radii along the diagonal and recover the square's side.

content.prompt: Circles of radius $6\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$ are placed in a square, as shown in the diagram. Find, correct to 2 decimal places:

spec.description: Two externally tangent circles in opposite square corners; B, E, F and D lie on the dashed diagonal. Red distinguishes the diagonal and centres. Redundant unused corner labels A and C are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The larger radius is 6 cm and the smaller radius is 3 cm. Each circle touches its two adjacent sides. EF=9 cm; the square side is 9+9/sqrt(2) cm.

answer.worked:
The radii to the top and right sides form perpendicular lengths of $6\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}EB^2&=6^2+6^2\\EB^2&=72\\EB&=6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\\EB&\approx8.49\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

The radii to the left and bottom sides form perpendicular lengths of $3\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}FD^2&=3^2+3^2\\FD^2&=18\\FD&=3\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\\FD&\approx4.24\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

The circles touch, so $EF=6+3=9\text{ cm}$. Keep the earlier lengths exact.

$$\begin{align*}BD&=BE+EF+FD\\BD&=6\sqrt{2}+9+3\sqrt{2}\\BD&=9+9\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\\BD&\approx21.73\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: the side length of the square

answer.worked:
Let the square's side length be $s\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}2s^2&=(9+9\sqrt{2})^2\\s^2&=\frac{(9+9\sqrt{2})^2}{2}\\s&=\frac{9+9\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}\\s&\approx15.36\end{align*}$$
The side length is $15.36\text{ cm}$.
